diagnostics.message: `data.local_file.cluster_bootstrap_state` reads `${path.module}/cluster_bootstrap_state`, but that file is only ever produced at apply time by the `local-exec` provisioners on `null_resource.cluster_bootstrap_state` (\"printf 1 > ...\"). Nothing in the configuration (no reference, no `depends_on`) connects the two, so on any run where the null_resource is re-created the data source is read from the pre-existing/stale file content and the bootstrap-node `count` decision is made against stale state. The data source should be ordered after (and modelled on) the null_resource that writes the file — note the current implementation is inherently circular because `aws_instance.bootstrap_node` consumes this data source while the null_resource depends on that instance, so the file plumbing itself needs restructuring (e.g. a local/remote state object) rather than a plain reference.

`aws_instance.bootstrap_node` boots with `data.template_file.bootstrap_userdata_script`, which passes `asg_name = aws_autoscaling_group.master_nodes.name` so the instance immediately calls the Auto Scaling describe APIs to find peers. That permission comes from `aws_iam_role_policy.asg_discover`, which is attached to the role the instance profile points at, but the only reference chain is instance -> `aws_iam_instance_profile.elasticsearch` -> role; IAM inline policies are attached in parallel with the instance profile and propagate asynchronously, so the instance can boot with an incomplete permission set. The instance needs an explicit ordering on the role policy (no attribute-based reference to a policy attachment exists).

The bootstrap node's user data performs Elasticsearch discovery via `ec2:DescribeInstances`, granted by `aws_iam_role_policy.elasticsearch`. The instance only implicitly depends on `aws_iam_instance_profile.elasticsearch`, and the inline policy is attached to the role in parallel with the instance profile with eventual-consistency propagation, so the first boot can hit AccessDenied. Nothing in the configuration orders instance creation after the policy attachment.

Master nodes launched from `aws_launch_configuration.master` are precisely the nodes that use the ASG-describe discovery policy (`aws_iam_role_policy.asg_discover` is created only when `masters_count != 0`), yet the launch configuration only references `aws_iam_instance_profile.elasticsearch` / the role name. Because the inline policy is attached asynchronously after role creation, the ASG (which waits for healthy instances) can start nodes before the permission is effective. Add an ordering from the launch configuration (or the instance profile) to the role policy.
